text:
Ryan: Heads up — 99p SSE latency jumped ~2.1x after the 2.17 rollout. Affected routes are toolcall-heavy (rerank + function calls). Holding rollout.
Marta: seeing same in perf CI: staging-perf-job #438 failed the latency gate.
ci-bot: Perf job 438 — latency threshold breached on 'chat-stream-toolcall' (p99 = 890ms, baseline 420ms).
Sandeep: I ran a quick flamegraph on one sample — stacks point to serializer.serialize_block -> sse_writer.flush_lock -> wait_on_kv_fetch.
Elaine: that suggests KV prefetch/eviction is contending with streaming writer. We switched batching heuristic in the merge yesterday, maybe it changed access patterns.
Devon: opened a bisect run on the release branch. Starting with the 5 merges between 2.16.9 and 2.17.0.
Ryan: note: kernel-autoselect change landed in the same window too — it can pick grouped kernels that buffer more before yielding. Could be interaction with SSE small-write path.
Marta: quick profiler snapshot attached — high time in `stream::serialize_to_sse` and repeated kv_cache.get hits (miss->prefetch) per token.
Sandeep: hypothesis: new batching coalesces requests so KV prefetch gets triggered under the SSE writer's lock, delaying flushes and making TCP writes burst and then get Nagle+coalesce delays.
Elaine: can someone repro locally with the new batching flags? Try: `BATCH_COALESCE=on BATCH_WINDOW_MS=12 ./dev/run_local_stream --toolcall-heavy`
Devon: repro locally with that env — p99 reg from ~380ms to ~820ms. Captured tcpdump shows clumped SSE frames.
Ryan: thanks. I'm going to roll back the batching coalesce flag from the rollout and re-run CI. If regression goes away we have a root cause signal.
deploy-bot: Rollout 2.17.0 -> paused by @Ryan (reason: stream latency regression).
Marta: meanwhile, I'll add a micro-benchmark that simulates toolcall+kv churn to the perf CI, so we don't miss this again.
Sandeep: also adding a small fix attempt: move KV prefetch off the SSE writer path (async prefetch + lock-free cache write). Quick patch here:
```
- let val = kv.fetch_sync(key);
- sse_writer.lock();
- sse_writer.write_frame(val);
+ kv.fetch_async(key).await;
+ let v = kv.read_ok(key);
+ sse_writer.write_frame_no_lock(v);
```
Marta: that change looks promising, but it touches cache invariants. Add a canary and run toolcall-heavy traffic through dedicated nodes.
Devon: CI rerun started (job 439).
ci-bot: Perf job 439 — warmup then run.
Ryan: if rollback + canary both show fixes we can revert the batching coalesce merge and rework kernel autoselect to avoid increasing buffer latency for small-frame SSE.
Elaine: logging: add counters for "sse_flush_wait_ms" and "kv_prefetch_wait_ms" to trace when we hit this in-prod.
Marta: noted — will add short-term alert on sse_flush_wait_ms > 50ms for toolcall routes.
Devon: bisect results so far: commit 8f3a2b4 (batching coalesce) correlates with the reg. Keeping running patch tests.
Sandeep: if coalesce is culprit, we should also consider lowering coalesce window or making it opt-in per-route (disable for toolcall-heavy).
Ryan: agreed. For now rollback is safest. Thanks all — keep updates in this thread, ping me if CI passes. :thumbsup:
Marta: will follow up with a short incident note for postmortem once we close the revert.
ci-bot: Perf job 439 completed — p99 = 430ms (within baseline).
Devon: rollback confirmed fixed on staging. Re-run on canary nodes next.
Ryan: closing rollout hold after canary validation. Will open follow-up ticket for per-route coalesce flags and KV prefetch decouple.
Marta: filing follow-up: PERF-1229 — SSE flushing vs KV prefetch interactions.
Elaine: adding owners for the ticket: @Sandeep (runtime), @Marta (perf CI), @Devon (deploy).
Ryan: great work.
